topSignals.title: Bloom Energy launches Power Connect — factory-integrated deployment system cuts installation time >40%
topSignals.text: — Announced August 19, 2026, Power Connect moves critical electrical integration work from the field to the factory: systems arrive pre-connected, pre-wired, tested, and ready for installation. Bloom claims this reduces on-site complexity, improves deployment consistency, and accelerates commissioning. The standardized design creates a repeatable, scalable model for large-scale AI data center installations. Stock initially dipped on the news before stabilizing; broader market reading is that Bloom is widening its time-to-power advantage over grid-based and SMR competitors. Bloom IR | DCD | Motley Fool

topSignals.title: Project Jupiter faces second NM Supreme Court petition — water use challenged alongside air permit stay
topSignals.text: — On August 20, the Center for Biological Diversity filed a second emergency petition to the New Mexico Supreme Court challenging the emergency water-well authorization granted by the Office of the State Engineer. Since April, >103 million gallons have been pumped from a new well without the required public hearing. The petition seeks to halt all water diversion until state law is complied with. Combined with the New Energy Economy air-permit stay petition (filed August 19), Project Jupiter now faces two simultaneous Supreme Court emergency proceedings. If either stay is granted, the September 14 NMED hearing cannot proceed and the November 23 permit deadline is missed, pushing first-power well beyond SemiAnalysis's 2029 base case. Center for Biological Diversity (Aug 20) | Santa Fe New Mexican

topSignals.title: PUCT August 20 outcome: ERCOT audit to complete by December; Batch Zero suspension confirmed
topSignals.text: — ERCOT confirmed at the August 20 PUCT open meeting that its comprehensive data-center verification audit (250-300 projects, primarily data centers) will be completed by December 2026. Batch Zero Large Load classification notifications — previously suspended August 7 — remain on hold pending audit completion. PUCT affirmed separate curtailment authority over co-located (behind-the-meter) data centers under Senate Bill 6. Key structural implication: fully islanded SOFC installations with no ERCOT interconnection remain outside the audit scope entirely and continue to be the fastest legal path to power in Texas. Houston Public Media | Baker Botts | White & Case

items.text: Elcogen (priority): Quiet day August 21. No new announcements. Status unchanged: E3000 G2 platform (>75% FC electrical efficiency, 90% with heat recovery, 650°C) in volume production at ELCO I Tallinn (360 MW/yr); EFCF 2026 embargo still holding. Recent milestones: EC Executive VP Teresa Ribera factory visit (June 2026), JNK India MoU (April). Elcogen newsroom

Topsoe (priority): Quiet day August 21 (SOFC/SOEC). Status unchanged: Herning SOEC factory hibernated post strategic review (May 2026); commercialization via licensing and demonstration partnerships; CEO Elena Scaltritti since June 1; FY2026 guidance DKK 7,600-8,400M. August 19 news: Topsoe signed a licensing and engineering agreement with Allied Biofuels (via Sasol partnership) — methanol/fuel synthesis, not SOEC. SOFC data-center commercial pathway deferred to 2029+. Topsoe.com

Bloom Energy: Power Connect deployment platform announced August 19 — see Top Signal #1. Stock trading ~$200-207 range on August 20-21, rebounding from ~$163 July trough. Q2 2026 record results (reported July 29): revenue $1.065B (+166% YoY), net income $196.3M (from prior year loss), gross margin 33.4%. FY2026 guidance raised to $3.9-4.2B (100% growth). Bloom Energy IR | 247wallst

Ceres Power (CWR.L): Goldman Sachs August Conviction Buy (168% upside forecast, see August 20 digest) remains the headline. Trading ~248 GBp as of end-August; down ~15% over August but outperforming the −31% July trough. H1 2026 results (September) remain next corporate catalyst. No new product or partnership announcements August 21. TheStreet

PowerCell + ECL + Bosch 300 MW H2 fuel cell partnership (new, July 14, not previously reported): ECL and PowerCell Group AB announced a strategic partnership for 300 MW+ of hydrogen-fueled PEM fuel cell capacity at ECL's AI data center platform, supported by Bosch (PowerCell's manufacturing partner and largest shareholder). Initial 35 MW deployment at ECL's CSC-1 campus in Santa Clara; balance (non-binding MoU) covers ECL's FlexGrid expansion in 2027-2028. Note: PowerCell uses PEM, not SOFC — a competing technology in the data-center fuel cell space. Morningstar/BusinessWire | Hydrogen Central

Project Jupiter (Oracle/OpenAI, NM, 2.45 GW Bloom): Two simultaneous NM Supreme Court emergency petitions (air permit stay + water well challenge) — see Top Signals #1 and #2. Legal escalation is now multi-front. Construction proceeding pending court response; September 14 NMED hearing status unresolved as of August 21. Center for Biological Diversity
Hedgehog Rice Texas (104 MW Phase 1): Construction reportedly started August 2026 per ERCOT filings. Fully islanded configuration means it falls outside ERCOT's Batch Zero audit scope. MLQ Research

PowerCell/ECL CSC-1 Santa Clara (35 MW PEM, 300 MW MoU): See Stack & Cell Technology. First non-SOFC fuel cell deployment at scale to appear in this digest — marks PEM entering the data-center fuel cell competition (H2-fueled, no NG pathway, lower efficiency than SOFC but faster deployment for green H2 scenarios). Morningstar
Crusoe/Cheyenne (900 MW Phase 1), Nebius/Bloom (328 MW NJ), Equinix/Bloom (100 MW+), FCEL/Fit Energy (380 MW): No updates August 21. Status from prior sessions unchanged.

PowerCell PEM 300 MW+ ECL deal: See AI Deployments. PEM fuel cells (H2-only, no NG multi-fuel flexibility) now entering the data-center fuel cell race alongside SOFC. SOFC differentiation intact: multi-fuel (NG/biogas/H2 blends), higher electrical efficiency (~60% vs. PEM ~50-55%), no need for pure H2 supply chain at scale. Morningstar

Background unchanged: Rolls-Royce SMR GDA DAC missed August 2026 deadline (now Q4 2026/Q1 2027 estimate); 13 hyperscaler nuclear deals >9.8 GW; solar+battery $25/MWh LCOE unsuitable for 24/7 AI baseload.

Bloom Energy (BE): Stock ~$200-207, +~130% YTD, rebounding from July $163 trough. Q2 2026 (reported July 29): revenue $1.065B (+166% YoY); net income $196.3M; non-GAAP EPS $0.78; gross margin 33.4%; FY2026 guidance raised to $3.9-4.2B (100% growth). Scandium class action: lead plaintiff deadline September 28 (class period Feb 27, 2025 – July 8, 2026). Power Connect announced August 19 (stock dipped intraday, then stabilized). Insider activity August 18: CLO Shawn Marie Soder. Bloom IR Q2 | 247wallst

Ceres Power (CWR.L): Goldman Sachs Conviction Buy (168% upside) from August; trading ~248 GBp. H1 2026 results (September) next catalyst.

lcoe.text: US natural gas spot price (August 21, 2026): Henry Hub ~$2.68-2.80/MMBtu range in late August 2026 (below 2025 average of ~$4.00/MMBtu). Implication: current gas price environment is more favorable for SOFC LCOE than the EIA $4.00-4.90/MMBtu forecast assumed in the model. At $2.80/MMBtu, SOFC LCOE improves by ~$12-18/MWh vs. base case, putting the low end closer to $110-120/MWh without CHP. Consider updating gas price sensitivity scenario to include a $2.50-3.00/MMBtu case. EIA STEO | TradingEconomics

Bloom Energy Q2 capex/revenue signal: $935.4M product revenue in Q2 2026 at 33.4% gross margin implies approximately $622M COGS on product. At ~$700-800M/GW revenue (carry-forward estimate), Q2 implies ~1.2-1.3 GW shipped in the quarter. Manufacturing scale-up is proceeding — watch for ASP trend in 10-Q (September 11) to assess whether price/kW is declining as volume increases.

Power Connect deployment system: Factory-pre-integration reduces on-site labor and schedule, which lowers the soft cost component of SOFC project CAPEX (permits, EPC labor, commissioning). Magnitude not yet quantified; watch for Bloom disclosure in 10-Q or investor day. Directionally deflationary on total installed cost.

PEM competitive pricing signal: PowerCell/ECL/Bosch 300 MW at 35 MW initial deployment. PEM for H2-fueled data centers at industrial scale is now an active competitor. PEM typically has lower capex/kW than SOFC but requires pure H2 supply chain and has lower efficiency. In the LCOE model, add a PEM H2 scenario alongside the SOFC NG base case.
